headline: Microsoft forms Xbox Labs to explore AI-powered game modding
summary: The new group will experiment with decompiling and recompiling games, embracing the chaos of AI-assisted game remixing.
details: Microsoft has established a new Xbox Labs group dedicated to exploring the rapidly evolving landscape of AI-powered game modding. This initiative aims to experiment with decompiling and recompiling existing games, allowing for new experiences and ports to different platforms.

Xbox CEO Asha Sharma stated that Xbox Labs will be a "small group of game makers, engineers and scientists whose job is to turn emerging ideas into things our players and developers can experience." The group will build in the open, learn from community engagement, and measure success by increased player and creator activity.

Sharma highlighted how recent experiments, such as porting Windows PC builds to Apple Silicon or running games in browsers, challenge traditional assumptions about the industry. These advancements decouple software from hardware and blur the lines between creation and play, offering new ways for players to discover and engage with games.

The move positions Xbox to play a significant role in the future of gaming, especially with the rise of AI agents. Sharma noted that coding was an early workload for agents, and games share similar properties, with players spending over 72 billion hours annually on Xbox games.

Xbox Labs will share its tools and learnings with developers. However, the company has not yet commented on potential issues regarding the unauthorized use of intellectual property when modders decompile and freely distribute modern console games.

headline: Apple TV 4K and HomePod mini 2 get hands-free Siri with new audio features
summary: Apple's latest streaming box and smart speaker get a Siri AI boost, enhanced home theater audio, and a remote finder. The HomePod mini 2 also gets a chip upgrade.
details: Apple has unveiled updated versions of its HomePod mini speaker and Apple TV 4K. The new Apple TV 4K focuses on bringing Siri AI to the living room for content discovery, allowing hands-free voice commands thanks to built-in far-field microphones. Users can ask Siri to play shows mentioned in messages or inquire about content details without interrupting their viewing experience.

The Siri AI integration on the Apple TV 4K displays responses in the corner of the screen as text only, ensuring it doesn't clash with audio from shows or movies. This clean implementation aims to provide information without auditory interference. Additionally, the Apple TV 4K remote has been upgraded with a sound-playing feature to help users locate it when misplaced, similar to finding AirPods.

The HomePod mini 2 receives a significant internal upgrade with the S10 chip, replacing the S5 chip from the 2020 model. While the full Siri AI capabilities won't be available at launch, this hardware upgrade is intended to support future features. For now, the speaker introduces 'Sound Glow,' which syncs lighting effects with audio, and expanded surround sound functionality.

A key audio upgrade allows users to connect up to four HomePod speakers with the new Apple TV 4K for an enhanced home theater experience, a significant increase from the previous limit of two for a stereo pair. This setup can provide more immersive, dimensional sound. The HomePod mini 2 can also be used as a stereo pair with Macs via AirPlay, offering an improved desktop audio solution.

The HomePod mini 2 is priced at around $300 for a pair, making it a more accessible upgrade option compared to the multi-speaker home theater setup. The new Apple TV 4K also sees improvements in its audio capabilities and Siri integration, aiming to provide a more seamless and interactive entertainment experience.
